cwe_name: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm

exact_cwe_mechanism.evidence: CWE-327 requires use of a broken/risky algorithm; this shows a timing side channel in scalar multiplication but doesn't demonstrate algorithm breakage itself

connection.evidence: Secret scalar 'd' is converted to binary bits; each bit controls conditional point addition operations, creating observable timing variations

diff_causality.evidence: This line introduces the branch condition that creates the timing side channel; reverting would remove the secret-dependent branching

security_control.control_requirement_evidence: CWE-327 requires secure cryptographic implementation; timing side channels violate this requirement
existing_controls_checked: No constant-time guards present in the scalar multiplication loop
security_control.deficiency_evidence: The naive double-and-add algorithm with secret-dependent branching lacks constant-time execution controls

concrete_impact.evidence: Timing side channels can enable private key recovery in cryptographic operations, but requires attacker measurement capability

diff_counterfactual: If the candidate line were reverted, the secret-dependent branching would be removed, eliminating the timing side channel in the scalar multiplication.
supporting_evidence: Secret scalar 'd' controls conditional point addition operations through bit-by-bit branching
No constant-time execution guards present in the cryptographic operation
The double-and-add algorithm with secret-dependent branching is a known weak pattern
contradicting_evidence: CWE-327 typically refers to algorithm-level weaknesses, not implementation side channels
The underlying elliptic curve mathematics may be sound despite the implementation flaw
unresolved_facts: Whether this implementation is actually used in security-critical contexts
Attacker's ability to measure timing variations in deployment environment
Presence of other side-channel mitigations elsewhere in the system
review_comment: The scalar multiplication implementation uses secret-dependent branching that creates a timing side channel. Each bit of the private scalar controls whether point addition operations occur, allowing timing analysis to recover the key. Replace the naive double-and-add algorithm with a constant-time implementation like Montgomery ladder that performs the same operations regardless of secret bit values.
